text:
alex (ceo): quick follow-up from todays all-hands Q&A. thanks for the tight questions — trying to capture a short decision set for teams.

mira (vp-product): can we get a compact, non-tech elevator line + a slightly nerdy variant for SEs? marketing keeps getting mixed signals.

alex (ceo): yes. please use these as starters (marketing, feel free to refine): Exec: "Redwood: inference that ships to production — predictable latency, lower unit cost, and one API across cloud, reserved, and private installs." SE variant: "Single runtime with workload-aware batching, KV prefix caching, and policy-based routing for predictable cost/latency."

sam (research): Suggest we add one measurable proof point line: e.g., "typical hosted p50 < 120ms; dedicated p50 < 60ms on reserved capacity" — helps when SEs get pushed.

mira (vp-product): thats useful. marketing: can you make a one-sheet with those numbers + an anonymized migration case study?

zoe (sales): for Q4 pursuit kits: should reps lead with Hosted trials or go straight to Dedicated for mid-market? we need the recommended sequencing in the playbook.

alex (ceo): recommended sequence: lead with Hosted trials for velocity. if latency, isolation, or contractual controls are deal-breakers, propose Dedicated as the next step. escalate to Private only for compliance-driven accounts. sales should keep the "trial -> reserved commit" cadence.

lee (cto): on prioritization: engineering wants a hard signal. propose a rule: any deal > $X ARR requiring sub-60ms p50 moves Dedicated perf work to the top of the backlog. product to publish the threshold.

mira (vp-product): noted. i'll publish a simple prioritization rubric and anonymized deal list for engineering leads.

marketing-bot: created task P-7721 in #marketing: "Draft exec + SE microcopy + one-sheet with proof points" assigned to @marketing, due in 3 business days.

alex (ceo): one more: when contrasting competitors, use contrast language like: "Where some providers focus only on model access or only on on-prem appliances, Redwood delivers a production-grade runtime plus operational controls across deployment modes." avoid naming other vendors in front of customers.

mira (vp-product): thanks. i'll post the rubric, the microcopy drafts, and the migration sketch in #product-ops. please flag any urgent customer asks there. :thumbsup:
